Its Design section covers the key (hash of the rust-toolchain.toml and Cargo.lock bytes), one baseline directory per key, a background refresh with an atomic rename, check runs copying the baseline into their per-job, per-side CARGO_TARGET_DIR, a fallback to an empty directory when no baseline matches, and isolation.

The Risks section covers a stale baseline, correctness of verification from a warm build (with a warm-versus-cold sample comparison), disk use, mutation through hard links, refresh contention, and cold start. findings.summary: The design leaves out the CI-result path that the checks stage already uses. For most jobs it would not shorten the checks stage it is meant to cut.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs lines 10-19: every job kind except build first asks for a CI result for the candidate SHA, polling up to the configured bound (athena.toml [budget] ci_wait_s = 1500), and runs checks locally only as a fallback. This job's own test check was reused from CI run 41829411253 (463 s). CI already keeps a target cache keyed by the same hash of Cargo.lock and rust-toolchain.toml (docs/design/ci-routing.md section 4.1, built per section 10 item 3). The note never mentions CI, ci-routing.md or routing; a search of the note for CI, ci_wait and routing finds nothing. It treats the review's premise that checks always build from an empty local CARGO_TARGET_DIR as fact, when the code at this commit could have been read. A local warm baseline helps only the local fallback path. A careful design would split the 14.1 minutes into CI wait versus local runs, using ci_result records, which give the source (CI or local) and the duration. It would treat the existing CI cache, or a warmer one, as the main alternative, and scale the 8.0-minute prediction to the share of runs that fall back to local checks.
findings.location: docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md (Problem, Why this removes the bottleneck, Alternatives considered)

findings.summary: The note overstates what a copied target directory saves: in a fresh snapshot every workspace crate rebuilds, not just the changed ones.
findings.evidence: From Cargo's documented behavior; I ran nothing to show it. Stable Cargo decides whether local path crates are fresh by file mtime. Content hashing (checksum freshness) is unstable, so 'compare source mtimes and content hashes' is inaccurate. Every file in a freshly checked-out snapshot is newer than the baseline's dep-info, so all workspace crates recompile and only third-party dependencies are reused. The claim that Cargo does not rebuild 'untouched crates' is therefore wrong, and the 8.0-minute estimate should allow for it. Also, requiring matching keys does not mitigate mtime quirks, though the note offers it as the mitigation.
findings.location: docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md, Design step 4, Why this removes the bottleneck, Risks: Stale baseline

summary: I'm failing this change on soundness, even though all five acceptance criteria are met. The candidate adds docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md and a CHANGELOG entry, and touches no other file. The note cites review 20261029-155931-wfkr and the measured figures (25.4, 14.1, 6.8, 2.5). It states the 8.0-minute predicted saving, labels its estimates, explains how the next review measures the saving, and lists alternatives and risks. The problem: the note never mentions the CI routing the checks stage uses today. For every job kind except build, Athena first waits up to 1500 s for the candidate's CI result and runs checks locally only as a fallback. CI also already caches build output under the same Cargo.lock and rust-toolchain.toml key the note proposes. A local warm baseline would only speed up the fallback runs, so the 8.0-minute prediction and the 'why this removes the bottleneck' argument rest on a premise the code at this commit contradicts. The note should split the checks-stage time into CI wait versus local runs, treat the existing CI cache as the main alternative, and scale the prediction to the share of runs that fall back to local checks. A smaller issue: in a fresh snapshot Cargo rebuilds every workspace crate, not just the changed ones, so the note overstates what a copied target directory saves. I only read code and docs; THROUGHPUT.md and records/ are not in this snapshot. The only commands I ran were git diff.
